Refresh-token rotation for the auth service

Issued access tokens stay valid for 15 minutes and are renewed with a single-use, rotating refresh token, so a leaked token has a short blast radius and replay is detectable — without forcing users to re-login.

draft 4 steps · 3 files 2026-06-16

01

Objective

Today the auth service issues a long-lived JWT and never rotates it; a leaked token is valid until it expires days later, and there is no way to revoke a single session. After this work, sign-in returns a short-lived access token (15 min) plus a refresh token that is rotated on every use. Done means: a client can transparently renew an expired access token, a stolen refresh token is detected on its second use and the whole token family is revoked, and an admin can revoke one session without logging the user out everywhere.

02

Scope & non-goals

In scope

  • A refresh_tokens table keyed by a family_id, with single-use rotation and reuse detection.
  • A POST /auth/refresh endpoint that swaps a valid refresh token for a new access+refresh pair.
  • Reuse detection: presenting an already-rotated token revokes the entire family.

Non-goals

  • Device/session management UI — deferred; this cut only stores the data it needs.
  • Migrating existing long-lived tokens — they keep working until expiry; no forced re-login.
  • OAuth third-party providers — out of scope for the first cut.

03

Approach

Reuse the existing jwt.sign() helper in src/auth/tokens.ts and the requireAuth middleware; the only genuinely new pieces are a refresh-token store and a rotation endpoint. The hard-to-reverse bet is the wire format and the family model: a refresh token is an opaque random string (never a JWT), stored only as a SHA-256 hash, tagged with a family_id shared across rotations. Rotating issues a new token in the same family and marks the old one rotated_at; presenting a token that is already rotated_at means it leaked, so we revoke the family. Getting this shape right now matters because clients and stored rows depend on it.

The token row shape, fixed now because rows and clients depend on it:

refresh_tokens
  id          uuid    pk
  family_id   uuid    -- shared across rotations of one login
  user_id     uuid    fk -> users.id
  token_hash  text    -- sha256(opaque token); never store the raw token
  rotated_at  timestamptz null  -- set when swapped; non-null + reused = leak
  revoked_at  timestamptz null  -- set for the whole family on reuse
  expires_at  timestamptz
  created_at  timestamptz

04

Steps

  1. Add the refresh_tokens table.

    reuses the existing migration runner in db/migrations/ — add db/migrations/0042_refresh_tokens.sql with the columns above and indexes on token_hash and family_id.

  2. Issue a refresh token at login.

    reuses jwt.sign() for the access token in src/auth/tokens.ts — add mintRefreshToken(userId) that creates a new family_id, stores sha256(token), and returns the raw opaque token. Wire it into POST /auth/login.

  3. Add refresh-token rotation.

    New POST /auth/refresh in src/auth/routes.ts: look up by token_hash, reject if expired/revoked, mark rotated_at, and issue a new access+refresh pair in the same family.

  4. Detect reuse and revoke the family.

    In the same handler: if the presented token already has rotated_at set, set revoked_at on every row sharing its family_id and return 401. This is the leak-detection path from the diagram.

05

Risks

  • Clock skew across instances — a token near its expires_at may be accepted on one node and rejected on another. Mitigate with a small grace window and UTC-only comparisons.
  • Token leak via logs — the raw refresh token must never be logged or stored. Mitigate: store only sha256, scrub request bodies in the logger, and assert it in the test below.
  • Race on concurrent refresh — two parallel refreshes with the same token could both rotate. Mitigate: rotate inside a transaction with a row lock on the token id.

06

Verification

Beyond unit tests for mintRefreshToken and the rotation handler, run the end-to-end leak scenario against a fresh test DB.

Smoke test
npm run test:e2e -- auth-refresh — log in, refresh once (expect a new pair), then replay the first refresh token and assert a 401 plus revoked_at set on every row in the family. Confirm no raw token appears in captured logs.

07

Open questions

Two decisions would change the data model or client behavior if answered differently.

QuestionRecommended default
Refresh-token lifetime?30 days, sliding. Long enough to avoid weekly re-login; rotation keeps the blast radius small.
Where does the client store the refresh token?httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie. Keeps it out of JS reach; revisit if a non-browser client appears.
